**Methane Watch brief: Recurring methane near Yangquan City, Shanxi Province, China** (draft `brief-20261022T201112-8e9912`, not filed)

Site: near Yangquan City, Shanxi Province, China (37.8938, 113.5625); tipped by the Shanxi and Ordos coal basins (China) watch area.
Looks: 4 of 8 passes read since 2025-01-01 are candidates; EMIT looked 28 times in all.

- TROPOMI recorded a 14-day median anomaly of +124.7 ppb above background at this site (2026-10-06 to 2026-10-20), the highest of all nine watch areas scanned.
- EMIT read 8 passes since 2025-01-01 and found 4 candidate passes (2025-08-18, 2025-09-25, 2025-09-29, 2025-11-30); peak enhancement on the strongest candidate was 5121.5 ppm·m with 1224 pixels at or above 1000 ppm·m.
- The candidate window shows diffuse, scattered enhancement across the 6 km window with no single tight plume shape.
- EMIT looked 28 times at this site (2024-01-30 to 2026-08-17); NASA outlined no plumes here in the plume product.
- Carbon Mapper lists no plume within 5 km since 2025-01-01 (publication lag approximately 30 days).
- Check: VIIRS saw no heat source within 1 km over the last 30 nights; flaring was not observed (small or brief flares can be missed).
- Check: Overture Maps shows within 2 km: 1 pipeline (at the site), 2 industrial areas (1.8 km); nothing mapped for mining, waste, wetland.
- Check: The public registry (OGIM v3.0) lists no oil and gas facility within 2 km; a registry gap is not evidence of an empty site.
- Check: The nearest coal mine on Global Energy Monitor's record is Yangquan No. 1 Coal Mine (operating), 4.2 km away; owners of record Yangquan Coal Industry Group (100%); parent of record Huayang New Material Technology Group; 6 other mines on its record within 10 km.
- Independent detections: Carbon Mapper lists no methane plume within 5 km since 2025-01-01. Source: Carbon Mapper (data.carbonmapper.org).

| Hypothesis (unconfirmed) | Assessment | What would confirm or rule it out |
|---|---|---|
| Routine venting | possible | Repeated candidate passes on new dates with consistent spatial pattern would support routine venting. |
| Equipment failure or leak | possible | A single high-enhancement pass not repeated on adjacent dates would support an equipment failure. |
| Maintenance blowdown | possible | A candidate pass coinciding with a known maintenance window would support a blowdown. |
| Unlit or malfunctioning flare | cannot assess | A flare stack mapped within 1 km with no VIIRS heat on the same night would support an unlit flare. |
| Non-oil-and-gas source (landfill, coal, agriculture) | possible | Aircraft or ground survey confirming coal mine ventilation shafts within the enhancement footprint would support a coal source. |

Confidence that methane recurs at this site: moderate. Confidence in any single explanation: low without a ground or aircraft check.
